title: Human RPL7 and DDX21 function synergistically with HTLV-1 Gag to overcome genomic RNA structural barriers that block tRNAPro primer annealing.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the complete Europe PMC supplement (1.68 MB): it contains exactly one PDF (gkag680_supplemental_file.pdf, 19 pages) plus 22 figure images, and no tabular files at all. I extracted the text of all 19 PDF pages. The only machine-usable tables are Supplementary Table S1 (PCR primer sequences), Table S2 (three RNA sequences: 98-nt wild-type primer-binding-site RNA, 88-nt deletion mutant, 75-nt tRNA-Proline), and Table S3 (the complete affinity-purification mass-spectrometry hit list, ~63 rows of gene symbol + protein name + spectrum count in Gag-GFP versus GFP control). I also searched the full open-access text for any repository deposition and found none (no ProteomeXchange, PRIDE or MassIVE identifier; Europe PMC reports no cross-references and no text-mined accessions).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The gel-shift annealing kinetics (rate constant k, maximum fraction annealed, scaled rate k') exist only as roughly a dozen numbers typeset in main-text Tables 1-2 and as gel images; I read those numbers but there is no underlying data file. The claim that the mass-spectrometry experiment used one Gag-GFP pull-down and one GFP control pull-down comes from the Methods text, not from a raw file.

a1_downloadable.note: Data availability statement reads: 'All data described are contained within the article. Requests to access the datasets should be directed to K.M.-F.' That is explicit available-on-request. Nothing is deposited in any repository, and the only supplement is a PDF.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: In Supplementary Table S3 the measured quantity (spectrum count for bait versus control) is a column, so no construction is needed - but it is a column inside a PDF, not a data file.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are gene symbols only (63 of them) plus three RNA sequences given in full in Table S2; resolving 63 symbols to UniProt sequences is trivial, so this is not the failure point.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated throughout: total spectrum counts (dimensionless), protein concentrations in micromolar, RNA in nanomolar, rates per minute. Verified in the PDF and main-text tables.

a5_enough_rows.note: The largest table in the entire paper is the mass-spectrometry hit list at ~63 proteins (counted from the extracted PDF text). Other quantitative data: three RNA sequences and about a dozen annealing-rate measurements. Far below the ~400-row floor for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 1.68 MB supplement zip; the usable tables are a few kilobytes
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; size was never the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Main-text Table 3 ('top 10 AP-MS hits') matches the first ten rows of Supplementary Table S3 exactly (RPN1 50/4, RPL4 48/1, RPL7 25/0, DDX21 22/0). Internally consistent.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are direct physical measurements: tandem mass-spectrometry spectrum counts and radiolabelled gel-shift annealing rates. No model-derived or feature-derived label.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (an RNA language model) for the primer-binding-site RNA, or ESM-2 (a protein language model) for the interacting proteins
backbone.hardware: CPU only; embedding 63 proteins or 3 RNAs takes minutes
backbone.licence: Both backbones are openly licensed, but there is nothing here to fit a head on.

integration.partner_dataset: BioGRID or IntAct (curated protein-protein interaction databases) plus published HIV-1 Gag interactome studies
integration.join_key: gene symbol mapped to UniProt accession
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could a model trained on many published viral-protein pull-down experiments predict which host RNA-binding proteins a retroviral Gag protein will recruit - a question this paper's 63-protein single-bait list can contribute two rows of evidence to, but cannot answer by itself.

controls.positive_control: RPL7 should rank as a hit, because it is already known to help anneal tRNA-Lysine-3 to the HIV-1 primer-binding site; the paper indeed recovers it.
controls.negative_control: The GFP-only pull-down column in Supplementary Table S3 serves as the experimental background control.
controls.external_validation: Published HIV-1 Gag interactomes and the chronically infected MT-2 cell co-immunoprecipitations in this paper, but neither is a dataset we could score a model on.

honest_claim_h3: With these files the strongest honest claim would be 'among the 63 proteins that one streptactin pull-down of GFP-tagged HTLV-1 Gag from HEK293T cells recovered above background, a model can rank which are RNA-binding' - a statement about one experiment in one cell line, not about retroviral Gag biology.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence to predict which human proteins a retroviral assembly protein pulls down and which help load a primer onto viral RNA.
plain_idea.train_on: What I considered: one row per human protein recovered in the affinity-purification mass-spectrometry experiment, with its sequence as input. I verified the count: 63 proteins, with no deposited raw data and no replicates.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a protein is enriched with HTLV-1 Gag (a virus structural protein) over a control, measured as tandem mass-spectrometry spectrum counts; secondarily the measured rate at which that protein helps a transfer RNA anneal to the viral primer-binding site, measured by radiolabelled gel-shift assay for about a dozen conditions.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Retrovirologists would like a way to shortlist host RNA chaperones that a virus hijacks, which currently costs one pull-down experiment plus months of biochemistry per candidate; but this paper supplies too few measurements to train or honestly test anything.

ml_idea: The only machine-learning project this paper could support would be to predict which host proteins co-purify with HTLV-1 Gag from their sequences, or to predict transfer-RNA annealing rate from RNA secondary structure. Both die on sample size: 63 pull-down rows (one bait, one control, no replicates) and about a dozen kinetic measurements across three RNA constructs. The paper's real scientific content is mechanistic biochemistry - zinc-finger-mediated binding, synergy between RPL7 and DDX21 - which is reported as gel images and fitted curves, not as data a model could consume.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: the entire dataset is a 1.15 MB PDF whose tables I already extracted in seconds with pypdf; any model on 63 rows runs instantly on a laptop CPU.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows of the largest table in the supplement. I did it: Supplementary Table S3 has ~63 proteins, which is roughly one sixth of the minimum needed for even a classification task.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 and A5, both verified by opening the files. A1: the data availability statement directs readers to email the corresponding author, and nothing is deposited in any repository - the whole supplement is a single 19-page PDF with no tabular files. A5: the largest table is the 63-protein mass-spectrometry hit list from a single bait and a single control, with the rest of the quantitative data being three RNA sequences and about a dozen gel-shift annealing rates. This is a careful mechanistic virology paper whose results live in gel images and fitted curves; there is no feature/label table here at any size, and no amount of cleaning creates one.
